title: Per-head percentile clipping with layer-norm-aware rescale for model-specific quant calibration (Llama / Mistral / Qwen)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Objective: Reduce accuracy regressions observed after FP8/INT8 calibration on Llama, Mistral and Qwen family models by introducing a per-head percentile-based clipping step combined with a layer-norm-aware rescale stage applied during quant profile generation. This ticket owns the calibration workflow changes, validation harness updates, and rollout plan for the new profiles.
background: Recent calibration runs for several customer models show sporadic token-level regressions concentrated in attention heads with heavy-tail activations. Existing per-layer scaling under-reacts to head-localized outliers and causes downstream softmax instability for some prompts. Prior attempts focused on global layer rescale heuristics; those reduce some regressions but increase variance across seeds and prompt types.
proposed_solution: 1) Add per-attention-head percentile clipping: compute the 99.7th and 99.95th percentiles per head on calibration corpus and apply a soft clip (tanh-based) to values beyond the lower percentile bound to avoid hard truncation artifacts. 2) Compute a layer-norm-aware rescale factor: use running statistics of pre-LN variance to derive a multiplicative rescale per layer so that quant bins preserve relative magnitudes after clipping. 3) Encode hybrid profile metadata to support both FP8 and INT8 code paths (single source of truth JSON with flags for kernel selection). 4) Integrate into calibration harness with options: per-model thresholds, percentile window, and backoff schedule for aggressive clipping. 5) Add automated accuracy validation against held-out prompt suite and MBR-like scoring to detect subtle decoding drift.
implementation_notes:
- New calibration stage will live in calibrator/calibrate_headclip.py and emits profiles to /profiles/modelname/vX/headclip.json.
- Profiles include: head_percentile_p1, head_percentile_p2, soft_clip_alpha, layer_rescale_multiplier, compatible_kernels.
- Provide compatibility shim so runtime reads legacy profiles (backfill migration tool included).
- Add unit tests for percentile computation, deterministic clip behavior, and numeric stability across float-backend and quantized emulation.
- Performance: keep profiling sampling budget fixed; clipping applied only to calibration pass, not serving hot path. Runtime observes profile-supplied rescale factors only.
- Backout: feature flag runtime.quant_profile.experimental_headclip.
testing_plan: 1) Offline: run calibration on 5 model variants per family (Llama-2-13B, Llama-2-70B, Mistral-7B, Mistral-8x, Qwen-7B, Qwen-2-14B) and produce baseline (no headclip) vs headclip FP8/INT8 profiles. 2) Regression tests: compare token-by-token logprobs on a curated 2500-prompt holdout; fail if >0.2% of prompts degrade beyond 2 logprob points on average. 3) Decoding drift: run 100k sample generation check for distributional drift metrics (entropy, token diversity). 4) Canary rollout: start with 5% traffic on public hosted, A/B to legacy profile with telemetry hooks for latency/cost/quality; abort if quality delta > threshold. 5) PR benchmarks: integrate with perf-ci and nightly accuracy job.
acceptance_criteria:
- Calibration harness produces profiles for all tested models that pass regression thresholds in testing_plan.
- Runtime successfully consumes new profile schema and selected models show no latency regression >1% at p95.
- Canary runs for 7 days with no customer-visible degradation and telemetry confirms cost neutral for token throughput.
- Design doc and confluence page reviewed and approved by Applied ML and Serving Runtime leads.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: per-head clipping may over-attenuate rare but important signals causing subtle hallucination regressions. Mitigation: soft clip (alpha) parameter tuning and conservative default percentiles; run MBR-style rescoring and backoff schedule that disables headclip for models/workloads that show regression. Risk: new profile schema increases config sprawl. Mitigation: single JSON schema with explicit kernel compatibility flags and migration tool to convert legacy profiles.
